findings.summary: The two panels are drawn on independent x scales, so a count in one panel cannot be compared with a count in the other by eye. Measured on the attached PNG: the left panel's 711 spans x=267 to about x=629, about 0.51 px per name, so its 17 (x=267-273) and 16 each render about 7 px wide; the right panel's 15 spans x=939 to x=1179, about 16 px per sample, so it renders 241 px wide. The same counted quantity therefore reads roughly thirty times larger in the right panel, and a reader comparing the left panel's near-zero groups with the right panel's gets the ordering backwards from what the counts say. Separate scales are defensible because the populations differ (744 names against 20 hand reads), but nothing on the figure says the panels are not comparable. Line is null because the drawing script is not in the reviewed tree.

Colour carries no meaning a reader can carry across the two panels, and in neither panel does it encode a quantity the row labels do not already name. Blue is 'links one plant code' in the left panel and 'right' in the right; grey is 'no plant code' on the left (#C4C4C4) and 'undecidable' on the right (#929292); purple appears once, for 'code only inside a longer word'. So a reader who learns 'blue means the rule links it' from the left panel reads the right panel's five confirmed cases as linked names, which they are not in the same sense, and the two greys make the same conceptual 'not linked' read as two different things. The house plot style asks one colour per component kept constant across figures, and no per-row hue where the row label already names the row; both are broken here.

The 'no plant code' bar in the left panel is filled #C4C4C4, about 1.85:1 against white, below the 3:1 ratio a data mark should clear. Combined with the bar's 7 px length, the 16-count group is the faintest mark on the canvas and is easy to miss entirely at the size the figure is read at, while its neighbour the 17-count group is drawn in a saturated purple that stands out. Both groups are the negative control the caption says the figure shows, so a reader should be able to see that both are there. The right panel's grey #929292 clears the floor at about 3.05:1, so the same neutral is drawn at two different strengths.
